title: A fixed cohomology degree of derived tensor depends on finite truncation windows
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use the abelian category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor is the bifunctor computed by total tensors of K-flat resolutions with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $K,L\in D(R)$ and $b_K,b_L\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for $q>b_K$ and $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>b_L$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every $i\in\mathbf Z$ and integers $a,c$ with $a\leq i-b_L$ and $c\leq i-b_K$, the canonical good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves $$H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i((\tau_{\geq a}K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(\tau_{\geq c}L)).$$ The truncated factors have cohomology only in $[a,b_K]$ and $[c,b_L]$, respectively, with the interval interpreted as empty if its lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint. No Noetherian, local-constancy, finite-generation, or existence-of-points hypothesis is imposed.
